scope_note: Third corrective audit for the 143,439-square-foot IM3 Microsoft building footprint in Quincy, Grant County. Coordinate, assessor, SEPA and air-permit evidence place the footprint in Microsoft's MWH (formerly Project Oxford) campus at 1515 Port Industrial Way, not the separate Columbia campus at 501 Port Industrial Parkway that opened in 2007. Building allocation remains unresolved, but that does not erase publishable campus, company-county or Chelan-Douglas-Grant regional evidence. Every wider fact is retained at its true scope with inventory_allocation unallocated and explicit non-additivity: campus tax and equipment facts are not divided by floor area; regional operating, construction, supplier, tax and community figures are not relabeled as MWH or selected-building observations; source-modeled IMPLAN outputs remain modeled; supporting water and power infrastructure is not converted into private investment, utility consumption, public subsidy, marginal service cost or net fiscal benefit.

sources.title: Growing with the cloud—Quincy, WA
sources.notes: The operator describes two Quincy campuses with more than 20 buildings and about 2 million square feet. These current portfolio descriptors cannot identify the selected IM3 footprint or backdate it to the original 2007 Columbia opening.

sources.title: Grant County property account 72793 — parcel 313769000
sources.notes: The official portal identifies Microsoft Corporation real-property account 72793 at 1515 NW Port Industrial Parkway, parcel 313769000, with 152.91 acres, multiple separately dated improvements and annual value/tax history. Complete payment statements are 727932021 (tax year 2022), 727932022 (2023), 57704 (2024), 57524 (2025) and 57298 (2026). The account is campus-wide; its several 140,908-square-foot improvements do not match or crosswalk the selected 143,439-square-foot IM3 polygon. Taxable and appraised value are equal in the retained years and exemption loss is displayed as zero, which does not address state sales/use-tax preferences.

sources.title: Grant County personal-property account 84139 — Microsoft MWH
sources.notes: The official portal labels personal-property account 84139 'MWH - 1515 NW Port Industrial Pkwy' and supplies annual value and payment history. Complete payment statements are 841392021 (tax year 2022), 841392022 (2023), 61710 (2024) and 61472 (2025). It is kept separate from real account 72793 and from later MWH20/MWH21/MWH23/MWH30 personal accounts at M Street addresses. Statement 61153 for 2026 showed one $2,631,463.16 half paid and $2,631,463.07 due when reviewed, so it is not retained or aggregated.

sources.title: Microsoft MWH Approval Order 22AQ-E035 and technical support document
sources.notes: The current order identifies the MWH facility at 1515 Port Industrial Parkway and lists commissioning dates from 2015 through 2022. Its equipment tables contain 45 generators for MWH01/02 and 72 for MWH03/04/05/06, 117 total. Permit equipment and potential-emissions limits are not actual generation, runtime, fuel use or emissions.

sources.title: SEPA 201805050 — MWH03-04-05-06 Microsoft Data Center
sources.notes: The register describes approximately 950,000 square feet of phased MWH03-06 construction on about 212 acres at 1500 Port Industrial Parkway and an increase from 1.4 million to 1.6 million square feet on the Microsoft campus. These are proposal/campus figures, not a final selected-building area, spend or completion date.

sources.title: SEPA 202403581 — MWH08 Data Center
sources.notes: The register identifies a later proposed 455,000-square-foot, two-story MWH08 building at 1515 Port Industrial Way on parcel 042009305. It is evidence of continuing campus expansion and is excluded from the selected footprint and the older parcel account.

sources.title: JLARC Final Report 17-02 — Data Center Equipment sales and use tax preference
sources.publisher: Washington State Joint Legislative Audit and Review Committee
sources.notes: The review names Microsoft Corporation among statewide direct beneficiaries and reports that 12 of 15 beneficiaries through 2014 were in Grant County. It also explains that reporting defects prevent direct beneficiary-savings measurement. Aggregate savings, job requirements, REMI multipliers and fiscal scenarios cannot be assigned to MWH or the selected building.

sources.title: Grant PUD January 25, 2022 FYI packet — December 2021 contracts
sources.notes: The contract register reports a $4,807,473 awarded amount in parentheses for Microsoft Large Power Facilities Agreement 140-10532, covering Columbia CO5 and MWH3&4, executed December 7, 2021 with an August 7, 2023 completion date. Later registers still showed it open. Parentheses are consistent with a PUD receivable, but the register is not a payment ledger; the amount is retained only as a mixed-campus source projection.

sources.title: Microsoft and City of Quincy water supply and facility agreement with Addendum 2
sources.notes: The agreement distinguishes the Columbia facility from Project Oxford/MWH, defines Oxford phases and water rights, and anticipates approximately $10,469,601.82 for Oxford utility infrastructure subject to final design and bid cost. Its $62,728.85 monthly payment is expressly illustrative. Neither figure is normalized because the former may be nested in the later $31 million reuse-system record and the latter is not an actual bill.

sources.title: City of Quincy financial statements audit report, 2020-2021
sources.notes: The audit says Microsoft-completed reuse components and City-completed components coexist, while City financing is backed by Microsoft and repaid through rates. Fund and debt schedules are City-wide or project-wide and cannot be assigned to the selected building; they are not added to the existing $31 million EPA total.

sources.title: Economic contributions of Microsoft's data centers in the Central Washington region
sources.notes: The factsheet reports 377 Microsoft jobs in 2024, $2 million of FY2019-2024 community investment and $26.4 million of 2024 property taxes, but its scope spans Chelan, Douglas and Grant counties. It mixes onsite contractors with modeled indirect/induced jobs and labels construction jobs, labor income and regional GDP as impacts. Those broader and modeled figures are not converted into selected-building observations.

sources.title: Microsoft gifts $25K to BBCC Data Center Program
sources.notes: The public-college recipient confirms a $25,000 Microsoft Community Empowerment Fund gift for Data Center Academy scholarships. It is a Grant County community record but is not allocated to MWH or the selected footprint and may be nested in a broader operator total.

sources.title: Commission recap 6-11-2019 — Microsoft conservation rebate
sources.notes: The PUD says Microsoft forwent a conservation rebate, allowing $480,000 to be dispersed through a Pay-it-Forward program, and separately discusses systemwide Quincy transmission expansion. The recap does not identify the contributing campus, selected building, recipient payments or marginal service costs, so no amount is assigned here.

sources.title: City of Quincy 2018 budget — Microsoft Project Oxford Fund 450
sources.notes: Page 44 reports Fund 450 actual expenditures of $15,583,730 in 2015, $237,369 in 2016, and $816,693 year-to-date through November 30, 2017. The table also reports Oxford bond and note proceeds; financing receipts are not treated as Microsoft payments, subsidies or expenditure components.

sources.title: City of Quincy 2016 financial statements and federal single audit
sources.notes: The audited budget comparison reports $237,368.53 of actual 2016 Fund 450 expenditures against $852,873.49 finally appropriated. Note I defines Fund 450 as the account receiving and disbursing revenues and expenditures for design and construction of Microsoft Project Oxford infrastructure under Ordinance 15-457.

sources.title: Grant PUD November 26, 2024 FYI packet — October contract status
sources.notes: The October 2024 monthly contract report still lists 140-10532 as open for Microsoft Corporation, CO5 and MWH3&4, at -$4,807,473 with a December 31, 2024 date. The register is a contract-status table, not an invoice, payment ledger or selected-building allocation.

sources.title: Grant PUD January 20, 2026 customer rate workshop packet
sources.notes: The packet publishes proposed 2026 Large Industrial Rate Schedule 15 and directs qualifying New Large Load service to Schedule 94. It does not identify Microsoft's MWH tariff, meter, billing demand, kWh, invoice, payment or dedicated facilities cost.

sources.title: City of Quincy rate resolution effective through Resolution 26-755
sources.notes: The current City rate resolution publishes general utility, building-code and development fees. The public schedule does not expose a Microsoft/MWH account, metered volume, invoice, payment, Oxford cost allocation or marginal municipal service cost.

sources.title: Ecology PARIS facility detail — MWH08 Data Center WAR313961
sources.notes: PARIS identifies WAR313961 as active construction-stormwater coverage for MWH08 at 1500 Port Industrial Way through December 31, 2030. It confirms later construction and site responsibility but supplies no construction value, worker/payroll data, operating withdrawal, discharge volume, fee or selected-footprint crosswalk.

sources.title: City of Quincy service-line inventory
sources.notes: The inventory names Microsoft service lines for MWH03, MWH04, MWH05 and MWH06 at 1500/1515 Port Industrial Parkway and Road S. It confirms building-level water connections but provides pipe attributes rather than water use, wastewater discharge, utility charges or a crosswalk to the IM3 footprint.

sources.title: New Data Center Technician Career Launch Program Endorsed
sources.notes: The school district confirms Microsoft TEALS collaboration since 2017 and a career-launch pathway with Microsoft, Sabey, Big Bend Community College and other partners. It reports no Microsoft cash amount, participant completion, hiring outcome, campus allocation or selected-building contribution.

sources.title: Understanding economic impact in local communities
sources.notes: Microsoft explains that EY QUEST performed the local studies using IMPLAN input-output data and Microsoft-provided construction, operations, tax and headcount inputs. Direct, indirect and induced channels are defined; most jobs and tax effects are modeled, while some direct employee and contractor counts are company-provided. Labor income includes wages, salaries and benefits. Regional tax contribution is not equivalent to one municipality's retained budget.

sources.title: Grant PUD's conservation rebate paid forward by Microsoft
sources.notes: The PUD reports a $480,000 Microsoft-forgone conservation rebate: $470,000 contributed on Microsoft's behalf to Columbia Basin Foundation, comprising $400,000 for Big Bend Community College's Workforce Education Center, $50,000 for local produce and healthy-eating work, and $20,000 for school environmental education; the remaining $10,000 supported Share the Warmth. These nested components must not be added to the $480,000 total.

sources.title: Commission recap 10-25-2022
sources.notes: The commission recap reports Microsoft's $240,000 Pay-it-Forward donation associated with third-party-verified Quincy campus efficiency upgrades that saved 33.4 million kWh per year. The donation is Grant County community funding; the energy number is avoided use from upgrades, not campus load or selected-building consumption.

sources.title: Pay-it-Forward puts $58,000 to work in local communities
sources.notes: The PUD identifies $58,000 of 2024 Pay-it-Forward awards: $5,000 to the Moses Lake Boys and Girls Club, $25,000 to Share the Light, $2,500 for a Royal City police K-9 vest, and $25,500 across seven food banks. Program lifetime donation and award totals exceed $960,000 and $557,000 respectively, but they include multiple donors and are not attributed to Microsoft.

sources.title: 2020-22 Computer Science Program Audit Report
sources.notes: The recipient's program audit reports more than $70,000 of Microsoft equipment, approximately $180,000 of scholarships and $400,000 for Workforce Education Center completion across a five-year relationship. It also reports six scholars placed into internships, all hired into jobs paying $29-$34 per hour. The $400,000 is the same apparent Workforce Education Center transfer nested in the 2019 Pay-it-Forward account; the 2021 $25,000 gift may be part of the scholarship total.

sources.title: Grant PUD November 22, 2022 FYI packet — October contract closeout
sources.notes: The October register closes contract 130-11644 for Microsoft MWH03-MWH05 at a current value of $240,000 on October 3, 2022. The register verifies the customer, facility phases, identifier, value and closeout date, but not payer/payee direction, invoice detail, selected-building allocation or a private construction supplier payment.

sources.title: 2025 Microsoft Environmental Sustainability Report
sources.notes: The report says the Quincy Water Reuse Utility reduces Microsoft's regional potable-water use by 97 percent and makes 1.5 million cubic meters of water annually available for community drinking needs. These are conservation/system effects, not an actual MWH or selected-building withdrawal, consumption or discharge series.

sources.title: County Employment and Wages in Washington — Fourth Quarter 2024
sources.notes: The official QCEW release reports Grant County's 2024 fourth-quarter county context: 2,741 establishments, 41,480 covered jobs and a $1,254 average weekly wage. These county aggregates are not Microsoft employment, compensation or payroll and are distinct from annual 2024 values in the governed 2001-2024 county panel.

project_updates.title: Third corrective audit — Central Washington operations and source-model method
project_updates.notes: The 2025 Central Washington impact report and its methods page were reopened at page level. Direct, indirect and induced channels are defined; most job and tax-effect outputs are modeled, while selected direct employee and contractor counts are company-provided. Labor income includes wages, salaries and benefits. Retained at true scope: 377 direct Microsoft jobs in 2024; 287 onsite contract employees as a subset of 855 additional onsite/indirect/induced jobs; $93,000 average Microsoft-data-center compensation versus $53,000 average private compensation across Chelan, Douglas and Grant counties (reported 1.7x); $269 million annual regional GDP contribution; and two additional jobs per Microsoft job. The exact compensation proxy is 377 × $93,000 = $35,061,000 per year; because $93,000 is rounded, a $92,500-$93,500 sensitivity gives $34,872,500-$35,249,500. This is direct labor compensation including benefits, not observed payroll, Grant-resident wages, MWH payroll or a selected-building allocation. QCEW county totals and CBP establishment/industry routes cannot identify Microsoft, contractors or residents. The industry chart reports Security 200, Power generation/transmission 167, Employment/other services 114, Maintenance/repair 99, Retail 62, Healthcare plus Other 56, Restaurants 47, Other real estate 46, Support services 42, Professional/technical 31, Transportation/warehousing 17 and Manufacturing 3; these sum to 884, not the 855 headline, so the chart is preserved as an internal source conflict and is not aggregated or used to overwrite 855.

project_updates.title: Third corrective audit — water payload, reuse effects and regulatory ceilings
project_updates.notes: Microsoft reports that the Quincy Water Reuse Utility reduces its regional potable-water use by 97 percent and makes 1.5 million cubic meters per year available for community drinking needs; applying 264.172052 US gallons per cubic meter gives 396,258,078 gallons per year.
